title: Can herbage nitrogen fractionation in Lolium perenne be improved by herbage management?
journal: NJAS - Wageningen Journal of Life Sciences
source_location: Results and Discussion, 'On nitrogen basis' subsection, p. 174; reported mean nitrogen fractions for lamina and sheath.
geography: Teagasc Johnstown Castle Research Centre, Wexford, Ireland
material: Perennial ryegrass (Lolium perenne) cultivars Aberdart and Respect; lamina and sheath fractions; four sampling seasons in 2002-2003.
study_conditions: Factorial field study included nitrogen rates 0, 90, and 390 kg N/ha/year, regrowth intervals of 2-3, 4-5, and 6-7 weeks, and cutting heights of approximately 8 and 12 cm. The reported tissue means aggregate over management treatments.
measurement_method: Total nitrogen by Kjeldahl analysis. Nitrogen fractions follow the Cornell Net Carbohydrate and Protein System fractionation scheme; neutral- and acid-detergent nitrogen were also determined gravimetrically.
basis: g of nitrogen in each fraction per kg total nitrogen; the ten extracted rows reproduce the paper's rounded lamina and sheath mean values.
evidence_class: primary_literature_measurement; source observations are class B
license: Reuse license not identified in the accessed article record; verify before redistribution beyond this project.
activation_state: The reported B1N, B2N, B3N, and CN means are used only to form a GreenHub-specific relative allocation between soluble and non-soluble protein pseudocomponents. B1N is the source's CNCPS buffer-soluble true-protein fraction; it is distinct from BIN, the buffer-insoluble nitrogen assay used in fraction calculations. The derived GreenHub values are class C; source observations remain class B.

calculation.soluble_mass_share: 175 / (175 + 592) = 0.2281616688; the value 175 is mean B1N, not BIN
calculation.profile_mapping: Apply the same normalized share to Smit et al.'s 0.107 kg protein/kg dry roadside grass and convert to wet feed with the VARTA dry-matter fraction 0.143. Both model protein pseudocomponents use a 0.16 nitrogen mass-fraction convention, so the N-fraction ratio is used as a mass-allocation ratio.

limitations: Cultivated perennial ryegrass in Ireland is not the GreenHub Dutch roadside grass or the July 2026 VARTA sample.

The article's B1N label denotes buffer-soluble true-protein nitrogen; BIN denotes a separate buffer-insoluble assay in the CNCPS method. Buffer solubility under a nutritional fractionation method is not the same as recovery into industrially pressed grass juice; the mapping is a replaceable relative proxy only.
The N-fraction means differ between lamina and sheath and across season and management; their two-tissue average is not a GreenHub uncertainty distribution.
The SuspendedProtein model pool groups buffer-insoluble and cell-wall-associated fractions; it does not claim a measured physical suspension state.
GreenHub matched feed/juice/cake protein-fraction assays remain required under REQ-GH-P3-07 and REQ-GH-P4-01.
